samuel2.12.p1.b1.text: Then the LORD sent Nathan to David, …

samuel2.12.p1.b2.text: “There were two men in a certain city, one rich and the other poor.”

samuel2.12.p1.b3.text: “… the poor man had nothing except one small ewe lamb that he had bought. … it slept in his arms and was like a daughter to him.”

samuel2.12.p1.b4.text: “… he took the poor man’s lamb and prepared it for his guest.”

samuel2.12.p2.b1.text: “As surely as the LORD lives, the man who did this deserves to die!”

samuel2.12.p2.b2.text: Because he has done this thing and has shown no pity, he must pay for the lamb four times over.”

samuel2.12.p3.b2.text: “This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: ‘I anointed you king over Israel, and I delivered you from the hand of Saul.’”

samuel2.12.p3.b3.text: “Why then have you despised the command of the LORD by doing evil in His sight?”

samuel2.12.p3.b4.text: “You put Uriah the Hittite to the sword and took his wife as your own, for you have slain him with the sword of the Ammonites.”

samuel2.12.p4.b1.text: Now, therefore, the sword will never depart from your house, because you have despised Me and have taken the wife of Uriah the Hittite to be your own.’

samuel2.12.p4.b2.text: “I will raise up adversity against you from your own house. …”

samuel2.12.p4.b3.text: You have acted in secret, but I will do this thing in broad daylight before all Israel.’”

samuel2.12.p5.b2.text: “The LORD has taken away your sin, … You will not die.”

samuel2.12.p5.b3.text: “… the son born to you will surely die.”

samuel2.12.p6.b1.text: … the LORD struck the child that Uriah’s wife had borne to David, and he became ill.

samuel2.12.p6.b2.text: David pleaded with God for the boy. He fasted and went into his house and spent the night lying in sackcloth on the ground.

samuel2.12.p6.b3.text: The elders of his household stood beside him to help him up from the ground, but he was unwilling and would not eat anything with them.

samuel2.12.p7.b1.text: On the seventh day the child died.

samuel2.12.p7.b2.text: “… how can we tell him the child is dead? He may even harm himself.”

samuel2.12.p8.b1.text: Then David got up from the ground, washed and anointed himself, changed his clothes, and went into the house of the LORD and worshiped. Then he went to his own house, and at his request they set food before him, and he ate.

samuel2.12.p8.b2.text: “While the child was alive, you fasted and wept, but when he died, you got up and ate.”

samuel2.12.p8.b3.text: But now that he is dead, why should I fast? Can I bring him back again? I will go to him, but he will not return to me.”

samuel2.12.p9.b1.text: Then David comforted his wife Bathsheba, …

samuel2.12.p9.b2.text: So she gave birth to a son, and they named him Solomon. Now the LORD loved the child

samuel2.12.p9.b3.text: and sent word through Nathan the prophet to name him Jedidiah because the LORD loved him.

samuel2.12.p10.b1.text: Meanwhile, Joab fought against Rabbah of the Ammonites and captured the royal fortress.

samuel2.12.p10.b2.text: “I have fought against Rabbah and have captured the water supply of the city. Now, therefore, assemble the rest of the troops, … Otherwise I will capture the city, and it will be named after me.”

samuel2.12.p10.b3.text: So David … went to Rabbah; and he fought against it and captured it. Then he took the crown from the head of their king. It weighed a talent of gold and was set with precious stones, and it was placed on David’s head.

samuel2.12.p10.b4.text: Then David and all his troops returned to Jerusalem.
